text: Yeah, careful with that word. Because in the middle ages, that's not a joke.
That's a death sentence. Most accused were women, but men weren't safe either. If people think you
know too much about herbs, or you just look a little too confident while boiling soup,
that's enough. One bad harvest, one dead cow, or one neighbor who hates you. And suddenly,
you're the village witch. And once the rumor starts, you're in trouble. No one is looking
for evidence. They're looking for someone to blame. They'll drag you to the town square,
ask, are you a witch? And no matter what you answer, it's the wrong answer. Say no, and they'll say,
that's exactly what a witch would say. Say yes, and you've just scheduled your own execution.
The tests are even worse. One method, they tie you up and throw you into a river. If you sink,
you're innocent, but you drown. If you float, you're guilty. And they kill you anyway.
This was called a trial by ordeal. The idea was that God would decide if you were guilty.
Logic wasn't really humanity's strong point back then. 24 hours haven't even passed,
and everything is already falling apart. And this wasn't rare. This was normal.
Your ancestors lived like this for years, decades, and somehow they survived long enough
for you to be here. So yeah, say thank you, medieval grandpa. Every comfort you have
is built on a life he had to endure.
